app.name: Homebody
app.tagline: Home workout planner and load calculator

common.comingSoon: This screen is on its way.

chest.name: chest
chest.about: The pectoralis major. Brings the arms together in front of the body: presses, push-ups, flyes.

shoulders.name: shoulders
shoulders.about: The deltoids: front, middle and rear heads. Overhead presses, lateral raises and bent-over raises.

traps.name: traps
traps.about: Upper back and neck. Lift and squeeze the shoulder blades: shrugs, upright rows.

neck.name: neck
neck.about: The neck muscles hold the head and protect the cervical spine. Train them smoothly, without jerking.

biceps.name: biceps
biceps.about: The two-headed muscle of the upper arm. Bends the elbow: curls, chin-ups.

triceps.name: triceps
triceps.about: The three-headed muscle of the upper arm, about two thirds of its size. Straightens the elbow: close-grip presses, dips, skull crushers.

forearms.name: forearms
forearms.about: The forearm muscles are responsible for grip. They work in almost every pull and in wrist exercises.

abs.name: abs
abs.about: The rectus abdominis and the obliques. They flex and rotate the torso and keep it rigid in a plank.

lats.name: lats
lats.about: The widest muscles of the back, the ones that create a V shape. Pull the arms down and towards the body: pull-ups, rows.

middle_back.name: middle back
middle_back.about: The rhomboids and the middle traps. Squeeze the shoulder blades together: bent-over rows, reverse flyes.

lower_back.name: lower back
lower_back.about: The spinal erectors. Keep the spine straight in deadlifts, good mornings and back extensions.

glutes.name: glutes
glutes.about: The gluteus maximus, the strongest muscle in the body. Extends the hip: bridges, squats, lunges.

abductors.name: abductors
abductors.about: The gluteus medius and the hip abductors. Stabilize the pelvis and knees and move the leg out to the side.

adductors.name: adductors
adductors.about: The inner thigh. Bring the legs together and assist in squats and lunges.

quads.name: quads
quads.about: The front of the thigh. Straightens the knee: squats, lunges, step-ups.

hamstrings.name: hamstrings
hamstrings.about: The back of the thigh. Bends the knee and extends the hip: Romanian deadlifts, bridges.

calves.name: calves
calves.about: The gastrocnemius and the soleus. Calf raises, jumps, walking.

notes.lightestTooHeavy: Even the lightest weight is on the heavy side: do fewer reps and build up gradually.
notes.notEnoughWeight: Not enough weight for the target rep range: slow the lowering phase down to 3 seconds.
notes.bigStep: A big weight jump: fewer reps than usual for now, they will come back next week.
notes.tooManyReps: That is a lot of reps: switch to a harder variation or slow down, 3 seconds on the way down.

shell.notSaved: Storage is unavailable: changes will be lost when you close the page.
shell.saveFailed: The last change could not be saved.

loadError.title: Your saved data could not be read
loadError.body: Nothing was changed or deleted. You can start over with a clean profile, which erases the data saved on this device.

settings.intro: Any change rebuilds the plan immediately. Your weight edits and exercise swaps are kept.

scale.title: Overall load
scale.about: Raises or lowers the working weights of every exercise in one move. The calculator picks new weights from your equipment and recalculates the reps. Exercises where you entered the weight or reps yourself follow your numbers and do not change.
scale.label: Weights relative to the calculation

equipment.title: Equipment at home
equipment.about: The plan is rebuilt right away: exercises that need missing equipment are replaced with ones you can do, and the weights are recalculated.
equipment.listHint: Separate the weights with spaces or commas, for example 2.5, 5, 7.5. The calculator only picks weights from this list.
equipment.unchanged: The exercises in the plan did not change.
equipment.unchangedAdded: The exercises in the plan did not change: what is already there fits better, but new options are available for swapping and in the library.

settings.about: Exercises, photos and instructions come from the open Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). The calculation uses the Epley formula for the estimated one-rep max, prescribes effort as reps in reserve (RIR) and progresses weekly according to your training level. Homebody is not medical advice.

excluded.title: Excluded exercises
excluded.about: They are not used in any workout. Press one to bring it back.

sample.title: This is a sample plan.
sample.body: Body weight 80 kg, dumbbells up to 24 kg, three 45-minute sessions a week. Enter your own details and the plan will be recalculated.

plan.empty: Pick at least one training day in the settings to build a plan.

blockDone.title: Block complete
blockDone.body: Every session is ticked off. Press “Start the next block” at the bottom of the page: the new plan continues from the weights you reached.

nextBlock.title: Next block
nextBlock.pending: Press the button when you finish this block.
nextBlock.body: A new plan for {{weeks}} will start on the first Monday after {{date}} and continue from the weights you reached, including your edits. The overall load returns to 100%, counted from the new weights.

volume.title: This week’s load
volume.about: Working sets per muscle; secondary work counts as half a set. The marked zone is {{min}}–{{max}} sets, the optimal range for the “{{goal}}” goal.

photoShows.kb: The photos show a kettlebell and you have a dumbbell: the movement and technique are the same.
photoShows.db: The photos show a dumbbell and you have a kettlebell: the movement and technique are the same.

photo.open: Open the photos of “{{name}}” full screen

exercise.source: {{name}} · instructions from the open Free Exercise DB

rir.body: The weight is chosen so that after the last rep you could still do {{count}} more. If it felt easier or harder, enter the real numbers below.
rir.deloadBody: Fewer sets and about 90% of the calculated weight. Finish every set with 4 reps in reserve: your joints and nervous system recover before the next block.

session.warmup: Warm up for 5 minutes: skip rope or march on the spot, circle your joints, then do 10 squats and 10 incline push-ups.

card.explain: ≈1RM is the estimated one-rep max: the heaviest weight you could lift once in this exercise with good form{{perHand}}. You never have to test it. It is calculated with the Epley formula from the weight, the reps and the reps in reserve: weight × (1 + (reps + reserve) / 30). Today: {{weight}} × (1 + ({{reps}} + {{rir}}) / 30) ≈ {{result}} kg. This number shows your strength growing even when the weights and reps change, and the calculator uses it to pick the weights for your next sessions.

edit.hint: Change the weight or the reps to match what you do: every later session of this exercise is recalculated.

swap.done: Replaced {{from}} in every {{session}} session. Weights were recalculated.
swap.excludeHint: For exercises that are uncomfortable or painful. You can bring them back in the settings.

session.missing: This session is no longer in the plan.

sets.label: Sets
sets.hint: Tick a set as soon as you finish it: the rest timer starts.

rate.label: How did it feel?
rate.hint: The calculator adjusts your next loads.

session.failHint: If you missed several reps, enter how many you actually did in the field below.

missed.moveRest: You can do it today: the remaining sessions ({{count}}) then move {{days}} forward, and the order and progression stay the same.
missed.moveLast: You can do it today: the plan is extended by those days.
missed.skipHint: Or skip it and the plan carries on without it.
missed.skippedBody: It does not count in the plan. If you did it after all, restore it and tick the sets.

progress.subtitle: Estimated one-rep max, block {{block}}
progress.intro: Sets, reps and load for every exercise across the whole plan. The solid line is what you did, the dashed line is what the plan expects. Press a date to open that session.
progress.explainBody: It is the estimated one-rep max: the heaviest weight you could lift once in an exercise with good form. You never have to test it; it is calculated with the Epley formula:
progress.explainExample: For example, 20 kg for 10 reps with 2 reps in reserve: 20 × (1 + 12 / 30) = 28 kg. For exercises with two dumbbells it is counted per hand.
progress.explainWhy: Weights and reps change from session to session, and the 1RM turns them into one number for strength. If the 1RM grows, you are getting stronger. The calculator uses it to pick the weight and reps for every next session. Exercises without weight show a limit instead: the reps or seconds you could do to failure.
progress.empty: There are no exercises in the plan yet.

intro.overview: Tap a muscle to see what it does and which exercises train it.
intro.done: How you loaded your muscles in finished workouts. The hotter the zone, the more working sets per week.
intro.plan: How your current plan loads the muscles in a regular week.

map.norm: Target for the “{{goal}}” goal: {{min}}–{{max}} sets a week for a large muscle, fewer for small ones. Secondary work counts as half a set.
map.noHistory: There are no finished exercises in this period yet: tick your sets during a workout and the map lights up.

ranked.plan: Sets per week in the plan

detail.label: {{muscle}} details
detail.recovering: This muscle is still recovering: give it 48 hours before the next hard session.
detail.notInPlan: Your plan has no direct work for this muscle. You can swap an exercise in a workout under “Technique and replacement”.

library.empty: Nothing found. Try another search or filter.

body.intro: Weigh and measure yourself once a week, in the morning before eating, at the same spots. The weight on the plan start date sets your starting loads.

form.title: Add a measurement
form.hint: Fill in only what you measured. Use a tape without pulling it tight: waist at the navel, neck below the larynx, hips at the widest point of the glutes, arm and thigh at their widest point. Body fat is estimated with the US Navy formula from height, neck and waist; accuracy is about ±3–4%.
form.hintFemale: Fill in only what you measured. Use a tape without pulling it tight: waist at the navel, neck below the larynx, hips at the widest point of the glutes, arm and thigh at their widest point. Body fat is estimated with the US Navy formula from height, neck, waist and hips; accuracy is about ±3–4%.

body.needTwo: The chart needs at least two entries.

photos.title: Progress photos
photos.about: Take one every 2–4 weeks in the same light, pose and clothes. Photos are stored only on this device.
photos.errorLoad: The photos could not be loaded. Reload the page.
photos.errorSave: The photo could not be saved. Try another file (JPEG or PNG).
photos.errorSpace: This device has run out of space for photos.

backup.title: Backup
backup.about: One file with everything: profile, plan, edits, results, measurements and photos. Use it to move your data to another device or to restore it.
backup.exportFailed: The backup could not be saved. Try again.
backup.invalid: This is not a Homebody backup file.
backup.tooNew: This backup was made by a newer version of Homebody. Update the app and try again.
backup.previewBody: It contains {{sessions}}, {{measurements}} and {{photos}}. Your current data will be replaced; photos from the backup are added to the ones you have.
backup.legacy: This file comes from the earlier prototype and will be converted.
backup.restoreFailed: The backup could not be restored. Nothing was changed.

reset.title: Reset
reset.counts: Edited sessions: {{edits}}. Replaced exercises: {{swaps}}. Capacities carried from earlier blocks: {{carried}}. Finished sessions: {{done}}.
reset.about: A reset removes your edits, replacements and carried capacities and returns the overall load to 100%. Everything is calculated again from your profile. Finished sessions stay.
reset.eraseAbout: Erasing removes everything stored on this device, including results, measurements and photos. Save a backup first if you may want it back.
